overall: The AG found neither the Cape Light Compact board nor the CVEC board violated the Open Meeting Law when their chairs sent response letters to the Special Committee; the authority and misrepresentation claims were declined as outside the OML.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the regional compact's chair communicated with a quorum of the board outside an open meeting to get approval for a response letter, or held an unnoticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of evidence to the contrary, we credit the Chair's account, and find that the Chair did not communicate with a quorum of the Board members outside of a meeting, thus the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the cooperative's president communicated with a quorum of the board outside an open meeting to get approval for a response letter, or held an unnoticed meeting.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of evidence to the contrary, we credit the President's account and find that the President did not communicate with a quorum of the Board outside of a meeting in preparing and sending a letter on behalf of the CVEC to the Special Committee.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the chairs acted unilaterally without board approval and misrepresented personal views as the board's consensus.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern the authority of individual public body members to act, thus we decline to review this allegation and consider only whether there was improper deliberation by the Boards.

source.publisher_filename: DETERMINATION - 6 3 2013 - OML 2013-73 - CAPE & VINEYARD ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC..pdf
